10 A rock in deep space is travelling towards a distant star and collides with a stationary spacecraft.
What is not a possible outcome of the collision?
A
The rock becomes stationary and the spacecraft moves towards the star.
B
The rock moves away from the star and so does the spacecraft.
C
The rock moves away from the star and the spacecraft moves towards the star.
D
The rock moves towards the star and so does the spacecraft.
© UCLES 2021
9702/13/M/J/21

hints: Take the direction towards the distant star as positive, so the rock has positive initial momentum and the stationary spacecraft has zero initial momentum.
Use conservation of linear momentum in deep space where there is no external resultant force, so total final momentum must still be positive towards the star.
Add the signs of the final momenta for the case where both objects move away from the star and check whether a negative total can equal the positive initial total.
walkthrough: Choose towards the star as the positive direction. Then initial momentum is $p_{initial} = m_{rock}v_{rock} + 0$, which is positive.
In deep space there is no external resultant force during the short collision, so total linear momentum is conserved: $p_{final} = p_{initial} > 0$.
Therefore the vector sum of the rock momentum and the spacecraft momentum after collision must point towards the star.
If both objects move away from the star, both final momenta are negative, so their sum is negative and cannot equal the positive initial momentum.
No other combination is ruled out, because a large enough forward momentum of one object can keep the total positive. This is option B

A.explanation: Total final momentum is still towards the star because the spacecraft carries forward momentum while the rock has zero momentum.

B.explanation: Both objects moving away from the star gives total final momentum away from the star, which cannot equal the initial forward momentum.

C.explanation: The forward momentum of the spacecraft towards the star can outweigh the backward momentum of the rock, keeping total momentum forward.

D.explanation: Both objects moving towards the star gives total final momentum towards the star, consistent with the initial momentum.
